# Final Project: ARIMAX model for Electricity Consumption in Spain

```{r}
serie=window(ts(read.table("ConsumElec.dat"),start=1990,freq=12))
plot(serie, main="Gross internal consumption of electrical energy in Spain", ylab="GwH")
abline(v=1985:2020,lty=3,col=4)
serie
```

## A.1 Identification

### Plot Annual Mean(12m) vs. Variance(12m) Boxplot -> Stationarity: constant var for each level 

-> higher variance for at higher consumption level -> non-constant var: non-stationary
```{r}
m=apply(matrix(serie,nr=12),2,mean)
v=apply(matrix(serie,nr=12),2,var)
plot(m,v,xlab="Yearly Mean",ylab="Yearly Variance",main="serie")
abline(lm(v~m),col=2,lty=3,lwd=2)

boxplot(serie~floor(time(serie)))
```
Clearly, an increasing variance confirmed. Thus a log transformation applied to stabilize the variance!

```{r}
lnserie=log(serie)
plot(lnserie)

m=apply(matrix(lnserie,nr=12),2,mean)
v=apply(matrix(lnserie,nr=12),2,var)
plot(m,v,xlab="Yearly Mean",ylab="Yearly Variance",main="lnserie")
abline(lm(v~m),col=2,lty=3,lwd=2)

boxplot(lnserie~floor(time(lnserie)))
```

Then, variance seemingly constant!





### Month Plot -> Yearly Seasonality
```{r}
monthplot(lnserie)

plot(decompose(lnserie))

```
Clearly seasonality is present with s=12 months. Higher consumption in winter (for heating?). Higher again in July (AC cooling).

Eliminate the seasonality applying a seasonal difference.
```{r}
d12lnserie=diff(lnserie,12)
plot(d12lnserie)
abline(h=0)
abline(h=mean(d12lnserie),col=2)

monthplot(d12lnserie)
plot(decompose(d12lnserie))

d12d12lnserie=diff(d12lnserie,12)
d12d12d12lnserie=diff(d12d12lnserie,12)

# Variance:
cat("\nVar for D=0:", var(lnserie))
cat("\nVar for D=1:", var(d12lnserie))
cat("\nVar for D=2:", var(d12d12lnserie))
cat("\nVar for D=3:", var(d12d12d12lnserie))
```

```{r}
cat("\nVar for d=0:", var(d12lnserie))

d1d12lnserie=diff(d12lnserie,1)
plot(d1d12lnserie)
abline(h=0)
abline(h=mean(d1d12lnserie),col=2)
cat("\nVar for d=1:", var(d1d12lnserie))

# 2nd regular difference
d1d1d12lnserie=diff(d1d12lnserie,1)
plot(d1d1d12lnserie)
abline(h=0)
abline(h=mean(d1d1d12lnserie),col=2)
cat("\nVar for d=2:", var(d1d1d12lnserie))

d1d1d1d12lnserie=diff(d1d1d12lnserie,1)
cat("\nVar for d=3:", var(d1d1d1d12lnserie))
```
--> Seasonal difference is sufficient. For d=1 or d=2 the var increases again --> overdifferencing

MEAN CHECK via t-Test
```{r}
t.test(d12lnserie, mu = 0)
```
--> mean is significantly different from zero, so we include it in the models

```{r}
acf(d12lnserie, ylim=c(-1,1), col=c(2, rep(1,11)), lwd=2, lag.max=120, main=expression("ACF of " * B^{12} * log(X[t])))
pacf(d12lnserie, ylim=c(-1,1),col=c(rep(1,11),2), lwd=2, lag.max=120, main=expression("PACF of " * B^{12} * log(X[t])))
```
#### Seasonal Autoregressive Part P
We only take into account the red lags that are multiple of the seasonal period; for s=12, only lags 12, 24, 36, 48 and so on are considered.
PACF shows 2 significantly negative lags indicating the possibility of a AR(2) process. However, the ACF doesn't show a clear decay in the lags, only 1 strongly negative seasonal lag and after that no significant seasonal autocorrelation.
--> P=0,1,2 are still tried and let the AIC decide if suitable.

#### Seasonal Moving Average Part Q
ACF shows 1 clear significant negative lag --> Clear MA(1) model behavior with Q=1 and negative coefficient. No signs for Q=2, clearly insignificant.
PACF also shows decaying behavior with only 2 strictly significant lags with rather small values. After that still some small, but with 95% confidence significant value -> due to noise or AR/seasonal effects 
--> Q=0,1

-> in total ACF and PACF rather point to a SMA model than a SAR model. 

#### Regular Autoregressive Part p
- We observe a ACF with not clearly exponentially decaying pattern. Rather 1-3 significant spikes and then insignifcant.
- The first lags 5 are all significantly negative, only then the lags start to become weaker before they increase before the end of the due to the seasonal correlation behavior.
- Like in the SAR case, we still check all model combinations with p=0,1,2,3,4,5 while p=0 seems the most suitable from the ACF and PACF plots. Model with higher p are discarded due to the risk of overfitting and a preference towards parsimonoius models.
-->p=0,1,2,3,4,5


#### Regular Moving Avergae Part q
- PCAF shows a decay with the first lag of the ACF clearly being significantly negative. The second ACF lag is very close to 0 while the 3rd lag is slightly significant again. 
- This indicates a clear MA(1) behavior. We decide to also check the AIC for MA(2) and MA(3) 
--> q=1,2,3


### Conclusion:
We use the CLT to assume that the estimates are asymptotically normal distributed and check if the 95% confidence interval of the estimates overlaps with 0.

We see that the coefficient estimate for theta1 and Theta the 95% confidence interval does not overlap with 0. Thus we follow that the statement that these two coefficients are significant. The intercept is not statistically significant from 0, but with 95% confidence so small that we can neglect it and assume the intercept 0.

To systematically cover reasonable variants without overfitting, we want to test:

Non-seasonal AR (p):

Non-seasonal MA (q): 

Seasonal AR (P):

Seasonal MA (Q): 

Seasonal period: 12

Differencing: d = 0, D = 1

To avoid overparameterization (too many parameters relative to data), we’ll limit total parameters (p + q + P + Q ≤ 10) and exclude redundant/ill-posed combinations.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Define the models to test under the constraints
model_specs <- list()

for (p in 0:4) {
  for (q in 0:10) {
    for (P in 0:3) {
      for (Q in 0:4) {
        total_order <- p + q + P + Q
        if (total_order <= 10) { # restriction to prevent overparametrization
          model_name <- sprintf("SARIMA(%d,0,%d)(%d,1,%d)[12]", p, q, P, Q)
          model_specs[[model_name]] <- list(order = c(p,0,q), seasonal = c(P,0,Q), ParamCount = total_order)
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
results <- list()

# Fit all models with warning/error handling
for (model_name in names(model_specs)) {
  spec <- model_specs[[model_name]]
  status <- "OK"

  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch({
      arima(
        d12lnserie,
        order = spec$order,
        seasonal = list(order = spec$seasonal, period = 12),
        include.mean = TRUE
      )
    }, error = function(e) {
      status <<- paste("Error:", e$message)
      return(NULL)
    }),
    warning = function(w) {
      status <<- paste("Warning:", conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )

  if (!is.null(fit)) {
    se <- sqrt(diag(fit$var.coef))
    coefs <- fit$coef
    lower <- coefs - 1.96 * se
    upper <- coefs + 1.96 * se
    signif <- !(lower <= 0 & upper >= 0)

    results[[model_name]] <- list(
      Coefs = coefs,
      Significant = signif,
      AIC = fit$aic,
      BIC = AIC(fit, k = log(length(lnserie))),
      LogLik = as.numeric(logLik(fit)),
      Sigma2 = fit$sigma2,
      Status = status,
      ParamCount = spec$ParamCount
    )
  } else {
    results[[model_name]] <- list(
      Coefs = NA,
      Significant = NA,
      AIC = NA,
      BIC = NA,
      LogLik = NA,
      Sigma2 = NA,
      Status = status,
      ParamCount = spec$ParamCount
    )
  }
}
library(dplyr)

# Summarize results
summary_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(results), function(name) {
  res <- results[[name]]
  data.frame(
    Model = name,
    AIC = res$AIC,
    BIC = res$BIC,
    LogLik = res$LogLik,
    Sigma2 = res$Sigma2,
    Coefs = if (!is.null(res$Coefs) && is.numeric(res$Coefs)) paste(names(res$Coefs), round(res$Coefs, 3), sep = "=", collapse = "; ") else NA,
    Insignificant = if (!is.null(res$Significant) && is.logical(res$Significant)) {
  insignificant <- setdiff(
    names(res$Significant)[!res$Significant],
    c("intercept", "mean")  # exclude intercept/mean from filtering
  )
  if (length(insignificant) > 0) paste(insignificant, collapse = ", ") else ""
} else NA,

    ParamCount = res$ParamCount,
    Status = res$Status
  )
}), .id = NULL)

# Filter out models with any insignificant parameters
summary_table_filtered <- summary_table %>%
  filter(is.na(Insignificant) | Insignificant == "")

# Sort by AIC and BIC
summary_table_aic <- summary_table_filtered %>% arrange(AIC)
summary_table_bic <- summary_table_filtered %>% arrange(BIC)

cat("\nSorted by AIC (only models with all significant params):\n")
print(summary_table_aic)

cat("\nSorted by BIC (only models with all significant params):\n")
print(summary_table_bic)

```
### Final Model Choice

#### Model 1: SARIMA(2,0,1)(0,1,1)[12]

```{r}
(mod1 = arima(
        d12lnserie,
        order=c(2,0,1),
        seasonal = list(order=c(0,0,1), period = 12), #D=0 as we use d12lnserie
        include.mean = TRUE
))
```

#### Model 2: SARIMA(1,0,2)(0,1,1)[12]	


```{r}
(mod2 = arima(
        d12lnserie,
        order=c(1,0,2),
        seasonal = list(order=c(0,0,1), period = 12), #D=0 as we use d12lnserie
        include.mean = TRUE))
```
## A.2 Validation


```{r}
#################Validation#################################
validation=function(model,dades){
  s=frequency(get(model$series))
  resid=model$residuals
  par(mfrow=c(2,2),mar=c(3,3,3,3))
  #Residuals plot
  plot(resid,main="Residuals")
  abline(h=0)
  abline(h=c(-3*sd(resid),3*sd(resid)),lty=3,col=4)
  #Square Root of absolute values of residuals (Homocedasticity)
  scatter.smooth(sqrt(abs(resid)),main="Square Root of Absolute residuals",
                 lpars=list(col=2))
  
  #Normal plot of residuals
  qqnorm(resid)
  qqline(resid,col=2,lwd=2)
  
  ##Histogram of residuals with normal curve
  hist(resid,breaks=20,freq=FALSE)
  curve(dnorm(x,mean=mean(resid),sd=sd(resid)),col=2,add=T)
  
  # ACF & PACF of residuals
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  acf(resid, ylim = c(-1, 1), lag.max = 60, col = c(2, rep(1, s - 1)), lwd = 1,
      main = "ACF of Residuals")
  pacf(resid, ylim = c(-1, 1), lag.max = 60, col = c(rep(1, s - 1), 2), lwd = 1,
       main = "PACF of Residuals")
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  
  # ACF & PACF of squared residuals
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  acf(resid^2, ylim = c(-1, 1), lag.max = 60, col = c(2, rep(1, s - 1)), lwd = 1,
      main = "ACF of Squared Residuals")
  pacf(resid^2, ylim = c(-1, 1), lag.max = 60, col = c(rep(1, s - 1), 2), lwd = 1,
       main = "PACF of Squared Residuals")
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  
  #Ljung-Box p-values
  par(mar=c(2,2,1,1))
  tsdiag(model,gof.lag=7*s)
  cat("\n--------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
  print(model)
  
  #Stationary and Invertible
  cat("\nModul of AR Characteristic polynomial Roots: ", 
      Mod(polyroot(c(1,-model$model$phi))),"\n")
  cat("\nModul of MA Characteristic polynomial Roots: ",
      Mod(polyroot(c(1,model$model$theta))),"\n")
  
  #Model expressed as an MA infinity (psi-weights)
  psis=ARMAtoMA(ar=model$model$phi,ma=model$model$theta,lag.max=72)
  names(psis)=paste("psi",1:72)
  cat("\nPsi-weights (MA(inf))\n")
  cat("\n--------------------\n")
  print(psis[1:20])
  
  plot(psis,type="h",main="Psi Weigths - MA(inf)")
  
  #Model expressed as an AR infinity (pi-weights)
  pis=-ARMAtoMA(ar=-model$model$theta,ma=-model$model$phi,lag.max=72)
  names(pis)=paste("pi",1:72)
  cat("\nPi-weights (AR(inf))\n")
  cat("\n--------------------\n")
  print(pis[1:20])

  plot(pis,type="h",main="Pi Weights - AR(inf)")
  
  cat("\nNormality Tests\n")
  cat("\n--------------------\n")
 
  ##Shapiro-Wilks Normality test
  print(shapiro.test(resid(model)))

  suppressMessages(require(nortest,quietly=TRUE,warn.conflicts=FALSE))
  ##Anderson-Darling test
  print(ad.test(resid(model)))
  
  suppressMessages(require(tseries,quietly=TRUE,warn.conflicts=FALSE))
  ##Jarque-Bera test
  print(jarque.bera.test(resid(model)))
  
  cat("\nHomoscedasticity Test\n")
  cat("\n--------------------\n")
  suppressMessages(require(lmtest,quietly=TRUE,warn.conflicts=FALSE))
  ##Breusch-Pagan test
  obs=get(model$series)
  print(bptest(resid(model)~I(obs-resid(model))))
  
  cat("\nIndependence Tests\n")
  cat("\n--------------------\n")
  
  ##Durbin-Watson test
  print(dwtest(resid(model)~I(1:length(resid(model)))))
  
  ##Ljung-Box test
  cat("\nLjung-Box test\n")
  print(t(apply(matrix(c(1:4,(1:4)*s)),1,function(el) {
    te=Box.test(resid(model),type="Ljung-Box",lag=el)
    c(lag=(te$parameter),statistic=te$statistic[[1]],p.value=te$p.value)})))
  
  #Sample ACF vs. Teoric ACF
  par(mfrow=c(2,2),mar=c(3,3,3,3))
  acf(dades, ylim=c(-1,1) ,lag.max=36,main="Sample ACF")
  
  plot(ARMAacf(model$model$phi,model$model$theta,lag.max=36),ylim=c(-1,1), 
       type="h",xlab="Lag",  ylab="", main="Theoretical ACF")
  abline(h=0)
  
  #Sample PACF vs. Teoric PACF
  pacf(dades, ylim=c(-1,1) ,lag.max=36,main="Sample PACF")
  
  plot(ARMAacf(model$model$phi,model$model$theta,lag.max=36, pacf=T),ylim=c(-1,1),
       type="h", xlab="Lag", ylab="", main="Theoretical PACF")
  abline(h=0)
  par(mfrow=c(1,1))
}
################# Fi Validación #################################
```

```{r}
check_stationarity_invertibility <- function(model, label = "Model") {
  cat("\n========== ", label, " ==========\n")

  # Stationarity (Causality) check
  ar_roots <- Mod(polyroot(c(1, -model$model$phi)))
  cat("\nModulus of AR Roots (Stationarity):\n", ar_roots, "\n")
  if (all(ar_roots > 1)) {
    cat("=> AR part is STATIONARY (causal)\n")
  } else {
    cat("=> AR part is NOT stationary!\n")
  }

  # Invertibility check
  ma_roots <- Mod(polyroot(c(1, model$model$theta)))
  cat("\nModulus of MA Roots (Invertibility):\n", ma_roots, "\n")
  if (all(ma_roots > 1)) {
    cat("=> MA part is INVERTIBLE\n")
  } else {
    cat("=> MA part is NOT invertible!\n")
  }

  # Psi-weights (MA(inf))
  psis <- ARMAtoMA(ar = model$model$phi, ma = model$model$theta, lag.max = 72)
  names(psis) <- paste("psi", 1:72)
  cat("\nPsi-weights (MA(inf)):\n")
  print(psis[1:20])
  plot(psis, type = "h", main = paste("Psi Weights -", label))

  # Pi-weights (AR(inf))
  pis <- -ARMAtoMA(ar = -model$model$theta, ma = -model$model$phi, lag.max = 72)
  names(pis) <- paste("pi", 1:72)
  cat("\nPi-weights (AR(inf)):\n")
  print(pis[1:20])
  plot(pis, type = "h", main = paste("Pi Weights -", label))
}

```

#### Stationarity and Inveritbility

```{r}
check_stationarity_invertibility(mod1, "SARIMA(2,0,1)(0,1,1)")
```
